16	
17	# LaTeX 论文写作全流程
18	
19	ML/AI 顶会论文从草稿到投稿的完整指南。整合 Orchestra Research、VibeSkills、claim2evidence 三方最佳实践。
20	
21	---
22	
23	## 1. 工作模式
24	
25	开始前选择模式：
26	
27	| 模式 | 说明 | 适用 |
28	|------|------|------|
29	| **Build** | 从实验笔记/结果/代码生成论文 | 新稿 |
30	| **Improve** | 改写已有章节，强化论证 | 修改稿 |
31	| **Audit** | 输出风险列表 + 缺失证据 + 修复建议 | 投前检查 |
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 2. Claim-Evidence 方法论
36	
37	**核心原则：论文是一个有中心贡献的故事，不是实验的堆砌。**
38	
39	### 2.1 一句话贡献
40	
41	在写任何内容之前，必须能用一句话说清贡献。如果不能，说明还没准备好写论文。
42	
43	### 2.2 Claim-Evidence Map
44	
45	为每个 contribution 建立 claim→evidence 映射表：
46	
47	| Contribution | Claim | Evidence | Table/Figure |
48	|-------------|-------|----------|-------------|
49	| C1: 方法 X 在 Y 上 SOTA | 比所有 baseline 高 ≥2% | 5-seed 平均，p<0.05 | Table 1 |
50	| C2: 消融证明 Z 是关键 | 去掉 Z 后掉 >5% | 消融实验 | Table 2 |
51	| C3: 计算效率 | 比 baseline 快 3× | FLOPs + wall-clock | Figure 3 |
52	
53	**没有直接证据支撑的 claim 必须删除或降级为 discussion。**
54	
55	### 2.3 章节起草顺序
56	
57	```
58	1. Introduction + Experiments（先确定 claim 和 evidence）
59	2. Method（评估问题稳定后再写细节）
60	3. Related Work
61	4. Abstract + Title（核心 claim 定型后最后写）
62	```
63	
64	### 2.4 Quality Gates
65	
66	投稿前必须通过：
67	- [ ] 前两段出现显式 novelty 声明
68	- [ ] 每个 contribution 有可验证的 evidence
69	- [ ] Abstract / Intro / Conclusion 的 claim 一致
70	- [ ] Limitations 真实且技术性诚实
71	- [ ] 审稿人两分钟内能识别 delta
72	
73	---
74	
75	## 3. 引用防幻觉（CRITICAL）
76	
77	**AI 生成引用有 ~40% 错误率。绝对禁止凭记忆写 BibTeX。**
78	
79	### 3.1 黄金法则
80	
81	```
82	IF 无法程序化获取引用:
83	    → 标记 [CITATION NEEDED] 或 \cite{PLACEHOLDER_verify}
84	    → 明确告知用户
85	    → 绝不编造看似合理的引用
86	```
87	
88	### 3.2 五步验证流程
89	
90	```
91	1. SEARCH  → Semantic Scholar API 搜索关键词
92	2. VERIFY  → 至少 2 个来源确认论文存在（S2 + arXiv/CrossRef）
93	3. RETRIEVE → 通过 DOI 获取 BibTeX（程序化，非记忆）
94	4. CHECK   → 确认你引用的 claim 确实出自该论文
95	5. ADD     → 加入 .bib 文件
96	```
97	
98	### 3.3 API 速查
99	
100	| API | 用途 | 限制 |
101	|-----|------|------|
102	| **Semantic Scholar** | ML/AI 论文搜索 | 1 RPS (免费) |
103	| **CrossRef** | DOI → BibTeX | 需 mailto 头 |
104	| **arXiv** | 预印本搜索 | 3s 间隔 |
105	
106	```python
107	# DOI → BibTeX（最可靠的方式）
108	import requests
109	def doi_to_bibtex(doi: str) -> str:
110	    r = requests.get(f"https://doi.org/{doi}",
111	                     headers={"Accept": "application/x-bibtex"})
112	    r.raise_for_status()
113	    return r.text
114	
115	# Semantic Scholar 搜索
116	from semanticscholar import SemanticScholar
117	sch = SemanticScholar()
118	results = sch.search_paper("attention mechanism transformers", limit=5)
119	for p in results:
120	    print(f"{p.title} | DOI: {p.externalIds.get('DOI', 'N/A')}")
121	```
122	
123	### 3.4 引用处理规则
124	
125	| 情况 | 处理 |
126	|------|------|
127	| 找到论文 + DOI + BibTeX | 直接用 |
128	| 找到论文，无 DOI | 用 arXiv BibTeX |
129	| 论文存在但无法获取 BibTeX | 标记 placeholder，告知用户 |
130	| 不确定论文是否存在 | 标记 `[CITATION NEEDED]`，告知用户 |
131	| "我觉得有篇关于 X 的论文" | **绝不引用** — 先搜索或标记 |
132

135	## 4. 顶会模板速查
136	
137	### 4.1 ML/AI 会议
138	
139	| 会议 | 页数限制 | 主文件 | 样式文件 | 必须项 |
140	|------|---------|--------|---------|--------|
141	| **NeurIPS** | 9 页 | `main.tex` | `neurips.sty` | Paper Checklist |
142	| **ICML** | 8 页 (+1 camera-ready) | `example_paper.tex` | `icml2026.sty` | Broader Impact |
143	| **ICLR** | 9 页 (+1) | `iclr_conference.tex` | `iclr_conference.sty` | LLM 使用声明 |
144	| **ACL/EMNLP** | 8 页 (long) | `acl_latex.tex` | `acl.sty` | Limitations 必须 |
145	| **AAAI** | 7 页 (+1) | `aaai_template.tex` | `aaai.sty` | 严格样式 |
146	| **COLM** | 9 页 (+1) | `colm_conference.tex` | `colm_conference.sty` | 语言模型聚焦 |
147	
148	### 4.2 系统会议
149	
150	| 会议 | 页数限制 | 模板类型 | 关键要求 |
151	|------|---------|---------|---------|
152	| **OSDI** | 12 页 (+2) | USENIX `usenix.sty` | Research / Operational 双 track |
153	| **NSDI** | 12 页 | USENIX | Introduction 预筛 |
154	| **ASPLOS** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 前 2 页快速评审 |
155	| **SOSP** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 可选 Artifact Evaluation |
156	
157	### 4.3 模板使用原则
158	
159	```bash
160	# 1. 复制整个模板目录（不要只拷 .tex）
161	cp -r templates/neurips2025/ ~/papers/my-paper/
162	
163	# 2. 先编译未修改的模板，确认能跑通
164	latexmk -pdf main.tex
165	
166	# 3. 逐章替换内容，频繁编译
167	```
168	
169	**禁止事项：**
170	- 不要修改 `.sty` 文件
171	- 不要在会议模板间复制 `\usepackage` 行
172	- 不要只复制 `.tex` 而不带 `.sty/.bst`
173

175	
176	## 5. 写作规范
177	
178	### 5.1 时间分配（Neel Nanda）
179	
180	花**大致相等**的时间在：
181	1. Abstract
182	2. Introduction
183	3. 图表
184	4. **其余所有内容加起来**
185	
186	审稿人读论文的顺序：标题 → 摘要 → 引言 → 图表 → 也许正文。
187	
188	### 5.2 Abstract 五句法（Sebastian Farquhar）
189	
190	```
191	1. 你做了什么（"We introduce/prove/demonstrate..."）
192	2. 为什么这很难且重要
193	3. 怎么做的（含专业关键词以便检索）
194	4. 有什么证据
195	5. 最惊人的数字/结果
196	```
197	
198	删除一切泛泛的开头：~~"Large language models have achieved remarkable success..."~~
199	
200	### 5.3 句子级清晰度（Gopen & Swan）
201	
202	| 原则 | 规则 |
203	|------|------|
204	| 主谓紧邻 | 不要在主语和动词之间插入长从句 |
205	| 重点在句尾 | 把关键数字/结论放在句末 |
206	| 旧信息在前 | 先放读者已知的内容，再引入新概念 |
207	| 动词表达动作 | "We analyzed" 而非 "We performed an analysis" |
208	
209	### 5.4 常见修改
210	
211	| 问题 | 修复 |
212	|------|------|
213	| Abstract 太泛 | 删第一句（如果它能放在任何 ML 论文前面） |
214	| Introduction 超 1.5 页 | 背景挪到 Related Work |
215	| 实验没有显式 claim | 每个实验前加 "This tests whether..." |
216	| 缺统计显著性 | 加 error bars + 运行次数 + 计算方法 |
217

219	
220	## 6. 投稿工程链
221	
222	### 6.1 构建
223	
224	```bash
225	# 推荐：latexmk 一键构建
226	latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex
227	
228	# 手动：需要多次编译
229	pdflatex main.tex && bibtex main && pdflatex main.tex && pdflatex main.tex
230	```
231	
232	### 6.2 Lint + 格式化
233	
234	```bash
235	# Lint: 检查常见 LaTeX 问题
236	chktex main.tex
237	
238	# 格式化: 减少 diff 噪声
239	latexindent -w main.tex
240	```
241	
242	### 6.3 图表格式
243	
244	| 类型 | 格式 | 说明 |
245	|------|------|------|
246	| 矢量图（plot、diagram） | PDF | matplotlib: `plt.savefig('fig.pdf')` |
247	| 照片/heatmap | PNG 600dpi 或 TIFF | 栅格图 |
248	| 表格 | `booktabs` 包 | `\toprule/\midrule/\bottomrule` |
249	
250	```latex
251	\usepackage{booktabs}
252	\begin{tabular}{lcc}
253	\toprule
254	Method & Accuracy $\uparrow$ & Latency $\downarrow$ \\
255	\midrule
256	Baseline & 85.2 & 45ms \\
257	\textbf{Ours} & \textbf{92.1} & 38ms \\
258	\bottomrule
259	\end{tabular}
260	```
261	
262	**图表规范：**
263	- 用色盲友好色板（Okabe-Ito 或 Paul Tol）
264	- 图内不放标题（用 caption）
265	- Caption 独立可理解（不依赖正文）
266	- 最佳值加粗，标注方向符号（↑ 越高越好，↓ 越低越好）
267	
268	### 6.4 投稿打包
269	
270	```bash
271	# 清理辅助文件
272	latexmk -c
273	
274	# 打包投稿
275	zip -r submission.zip main.tex *.sty *.bst *.bib figures/ --exclude='*.aux' --exclude='*.log'
276	```
277	
278	### 6.5 常见失败点
279	
280	| 问题 | 解决 |
281	|------|------|
282	| 图片格式混用导致编译失败 | 统一用 PDF |
283	| 字体未嵌入 | `pdffonts output.pdf` 检查 |
284	| Overfull box 过多 | 关键位置手动调行 |
285	| 引用缺字段 | 检查 DOI/年份/期刊名 |
286	| 超页数 | 用 `\vspace{-Xpt}` 微调，或精简内容 |
287

290	## 7. 会议转投
291	
292	当论文被拒或转投其他会议时：
293	
294	### 7.1 ML/AI 会议间转换
295	
296	| 转换 | 页数变化 | 关键调整 |
297	|------|---------|---------|
298	| NeurIPS → ICML | 9→8 | 删 1 页，加 Broader Impact |
299	| ICML → ICLR | 8→9 | 可扩展实验 + LLM 声明 |
300	| NeurIPS → ACL | 9→8 | 按 NLP 惯例重组 + Limitations |
301	| ICLR → AAAI | 9→7 | 大幅精简，严格样式 |
302	
303	### 7.2 转投原则
304	
305	1. **永远用目标模板重新开始** — 复制目标模板，迁移内容，不要合并 preamble
306	2. **只迁移正文内容** — 不复制 `\usepackage`、header/footer 命令
307	3. **根据审稿意见改进** — 但不要在新稿中提及旧投稿（双盲）
308	4. **检查目标会议特殊要求** — checklist、ethics statement、LLM 声明等
309

# LaTeX 论文写作全流程

ML/AI 顶会论文从草稿到投稿的完整指南。整合 Orchestra Research、VibeSkills、claim2evidence 三方最佳实践。

---

## 1. 工作模式

开始前选择模式：

| 模式 | 说明 | 适用 |
|------|------|------|
| **Build** | 从实验笔记/结果/代码生成论文 | 新稿 |
| **Improve** | 改写已有章节，强化论证 | 修改稿 |
| **Audit** | 输出风险列表 + 缺失证据 + 修复建议 | 投前检查 |

---

## 2. Claim-Evidence 方法论

**核心原则：论文是一个有中心贡献的故事，不是实验的堆砌。**

### 2.1 一句话贡献

在写任何内容之前，必须能用一句话说清贡献。如果不能，说明还没准备好写论文。

### 2.2 Claim-Evidence Map

为每个 contribution 建立 claim→evidence 映射表：

| Contribution | Claim | Evidence | Table/Figure |
|-------------|-------|----------|-------------|
| C1: 方法 X 在 Y 上 SOTA | 比所有 baseline 高 ≥2% | 5-seed 平均，p<0.05 | Table 1 |
| C2: 消融证明 Z 是关键 | 去掉 Z 后掉 >5% | 消融实验 | Table 2 |
| C3: 计算效率 | 比 baseline 快 3× | FLOPs + wall-clock | Figure 3 |

**没有直接证据支撑的 claim 必须删除或降级为 discussion。**

### 2.3 章节起草顺序

```
1. Introduction + Experiments（先确定 claim 和 evidence）
2. Method（评估问题稳定后再写细节）
3. Related Work
4. Abstract + Title（核心 claim 定型后最后写）
```

### 2.4 Quality Gates

投稿前必须通过：
- [ ] 前两段出现显式 novelty 声明
- [ ] 每个 contribution 有可验证的 evidence
- [ ] Abstract / Intro / Conclusion 的 claim 一致
- [ ] Limitations 真实且技术性诚实
- [ ] 审稿人两分钟内能识别 delta

---

## 3. 引用防幻觉（CRITICAL）

**AI 生成引用有 ~40% 错误率。绝对禁止凭记忆写 BibTeX。**

### 3.1 黄金法则

```
IF 无法程序化获取引用:
    → 标记 [CITATION NEEDED] 或 \cite{PLACEHOLDER_verify}
    → 明确告知用户
    → 绝不编造看似合理的引用
```

### 3.2 五步验证流程

```
1. SEARCH  → Semantic Scholar API 搜索关键词
2. VERIFY  → 至少 2 个来源确认论文存在（S2 + arXiv/CrossRef）
3. RETRIEVE → 通过 DOI 获取 BibTeX（程序化，非记忆）
4. CHECK   → 确认你引用的 claim 确实出自该论文
5. ADD     → 加入 .bib 文件
```

### 3.3 API 速查

| API | 用途 | 限制 |
|-----|------|------|
| **Semantic Scholar** | ML/AI 论文搜索 | 1 RPS (免费) |
| **CrossRef** | DOI → BibTeX | 需 mailto 头 |
| **arXiv** | 预印本搜索 | 3s 间隔 |

```python
# DOI → BibTeX（最可靠的方式）
import requests
def doi_to_bibtex(doi: str) -> str:
    r = requests.get(f"https://doi.org/{doi}",
                     headers={"Accept": "application/x-bibtex"})
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.text

# Semantic Scholar 搜索
from semanticscholar import SemanticScholar
sch = SemanticScholar()
results = sch.search_paper("attention mechanism transformers", limit=5)
for p in results:
    print(f"{p.title} | DOI: {p.externalIds.get('DOI', 'N/A')}")
```

### 3.4 引用处理规则

| 情况 | 处理 |
|------|------|
| 找到论文 + DOI + BibTeX | 直接用 |
| 找到论文，无 DOI | 用 arXiv BibTeX |
| 论文存在但无法获取 BibTeX | 标记 placeholder，告知用户 |
| 不确定论文是否存在 | 标记 `[CITATION NEEDED]`，告知用户 |
| "我觉得有篇关于 X 的论文" | **绝不引用** — 先搜索或标记 |

## 4. 顶会模板速查

### 4.1 ML/AI 会议

| 会议 | 页数限制 | 主文件 | 样式文件 | 必须项 |
|------|---------|--------|---------|--------|
| **NeurIPS** | 9 页 | `main.tex` | `neurips.sty` | Paper Checklist |
| **ICML** | 8 页 (+1 camera-ready) | `example_paper.tex` | `icml2026.sty` | Broader Impact |
| **ICLR** | 9 页 (+1) | `iclr_conference.tex` | `iclr_conference.sty` | LLM 使用声明 |
| **ACL/EMNLP** | 8 页 (long) | `acl_latex.tex` | `acl.sty` | Limitations 必须 |
| **AAAI** | 7 页 (+1) | `aaai_template.tex` | `aaai.sty` | 严格样式 |
| **COLM** | 9 页 (+1) | `colm_conference.tex` | `colm_conference.sty` | 语言模型聚焦 |

### 4.2 系统会议

| 会议 | 页数限制 | 模板类型 | 关键要求 |
|------|---------|---------|---------|
| **OSDI** | 12 页 (+2) | USENIX `usenix.sty` | Research / Operational 双 track |
| **NSDI** | 12 页 | USENIX | Introduction 预筛 |
| **ASPLOS** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 前 2 页快速评审 |
| **SOSP** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 可选 Artifact Evaluation |

### 4.3 模板使用原则

```bash
# 1. 复制整个模板目录（不要只拷 .tex）
cp -r templates/neurips2025/ ~/papers/my-paper/

# 2. 先编译未修改的模板，确认能跑通
latexmk -pdf main.tex

# 3. 逐章替换内容，频繁编译
```

**禁止事项：**
- 不要修改 `.sty` 文件
- 不要在会议模板间复制 `\usepackage` 行
- 不要只复制 `.tex` 而不带 `.sty/.bst`

---

## 5. 写作规范

### 5.1 时间分配（Neel Nanda）

花**大致相等**的时间在：
1. Abstract
2. Introduction
3. 图表
4. **其余所有内容加起来**

审稿人读论文的顺序：标题 → 摘要 → 引言 → 图表 → 也许正文。

### 5.2 Abstract 五句法（Sebastian Farquhar）

```
1. 你做了什么（"We introduce/prove/demonstrate..."）
2. 为什么这很难且重要
3. 怎么做的（含专业关键词以便检索）
4. 有什么证据
5. 最惊人的数字/结果
```

删除一切泛泛的开头：~~"Large language models have achieved remarkable success..."~~

### 5.3 句子级清晰度（Gopen & Swan）

| 原则 | 规则 |
|------|------|
| 主谓紧邻 | 不要在主语和动词之间插入长从句 |
| 重点在句尾 | 把关键数字/结论放在句末 |
| 旧信息在前 | 先放读者已知的内容，再引入新概念 |
| 动词表达动作 | "We analyzed" 而非 "We performed an analysis" |

### 5.4 常见修改

| 问题 | 修复 |
|------|------|
| Abstract 太泛 | 删第一句（如果它能放在任何 ML 论文前面） |
| Introduction 超 1.5 页 | 背景挪到 Related Work |
| 实验没有显式 claim | 每个实验前加 "This tests whether..." |
| 缺统计显著性 | 加 error bars + 运行次数 + 计算方法 |

---

## 6. 投稿工程链

### 6.1 构建

```bash
# 推荐：latexmk 一键构建
latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex

# 手动：需要多次编译
pdflatex main.tex && bibtex main && pdflatex main.tex && pdflatex main.tex
```

### 6.2 Lint + 格式化

```bash
# Lint: 检查常见 LaTeX 问题
chktex main.tex

# 格式化: 减少 diff 噪声
latexindent -w main.tex
```

### 6.3 图表格式

| 类型 | 格式 | 说明 |
|------|------|------|
| 矢量图（plot、diagram） | PDF | matplotlib: `plt.savefig('fig.pdf')` |
| 照片/heatmap | PNG 600dpi 或 TIFF | 栅格图 |
| 表格 | `booktabs` 包 | `\toprule/\midrule/\bottomrule` |

```latex
\usepackage{booktabs}
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
Method & Accuracy $\uparrow$ & Latency $\downarrow$ \\
\midrule
Baseline & 85.2 & 45ms \\
\textbf{Ours} & \textbf{92.1} & 38ms \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
```

**图表规范：**
- 用色盲友好色板（Okabe-Ito 或 Paul Tol）
- 图内不放标题（用 caption）
- Caption 独立可理解（不依赖正文）
- 最佳值加粗，标注方向符号（↑ 越高越好，↓ 越低越好）

### 6.4 投稿打包

```bash
# 清理辅助文件
latexmk -c

# 打包投稿
zip -r submission.zip main.tex *.sty *.bst *.bib figures/ --exclude='*.aux' --exclude='*.log'
```

### 6.5 常见失败点

| 问题 | 解决 |
|------|------|
| 图片格式混用导致编译失败 | 统一用 PDF |
| 字体未嵌入 | `pdffonts output.pdf` 检查 |
| Overfull box 过多 | 关键位置手动调行 |
| 引用缺字段 | 检查 DOI/年份/期刊名 |
| 超页数 | 用 `\vspace{-Xpt}` 微调，或精简内容 |

---

## 7. 会议转投

当论文被拒或转投其他会议时：

### 7.1 ML/AI 会议间转换

| 转换 | 页数变化 | 关键调整 |
|------|---------|---------|
| NeurIPS → ICML | 9→8 | 删 1 页，加 Broader Impact |
| ICML → ICLR | 8→9 | 可扩展实验 + LLM 声明 |
| NeurIPS → ACL | 9→8 | 按 NLP 惯例重组 + Limitations |
| ICLR → AAAI | 9→7 | 大幅精简，严格样式 |

### 7.2 转投原则

1. **永远用目标模板重新开始** — 复制目标模板，迁移内容，不要合并 preamble
2. **只迁移正文内容** — 不复制 `\usepackage`、header/footer 命令
3. **根据审稿意见改进** — 但不要在新稿中提及旧投稿（双盲）
4. **检查目标会议特殊要求** — checklist、ethics statement、LLM 声明等

---

## 8. 投前清单

### 通用清单

- [ ] Abstract/Intro/Conclusion 的 claim 一致
- [ ] 每个 contribution 有对应 evidence
- [ ] 所有引用已程序化验证（无幻觉引用）
- [ ] Error bars + 运行次数 + 统计方法
- [ ] Limitations 章节存在且诚实
- [ ] 匿名化（双盲审稿）
- [ ] 符合页数限制
- [ ] 所有图表有自包含 caption
- [ ] `.bib` 中无缺失字段
- [ ] PDF 编译无 warning

### 会议特定

| 会议 | 额外要求 |
|------|---------|
| NeurIPS | 16 项 Paper Checklist（附录，不计页数） |
| ICML | Broader Impact Statement |
| ICLR | LLM 使用声明 |
| ACL/EMNLP | Limitations 章节（必须），Ethics Statement |
| AAAI | 严格样式文件合规 |

22	
23	## 1. 工作模式
24	
25	开始前选择模式：
26	
27	| 模式 | 说明 | 适用 |
28	|------|------|------|
29	| **Build** | 从实验笔记/结果/代码生成论文 | 新稿 |
30	| **Improve** | 改写已有章节，强化论证 | 修改稿 |

35	## 2. Claim-Evidence 方法论
36	
37	**核心原则：论文是一个有中心贡献的故事，不是实验的堆砌。**
38	
39	### 2.1 一句话贡献
40	
41	在写任何内容之前，必须能用一句话说清贡献。如果不能，说明还没准备好写论文。
42	
43	### 2.2 Claim-Evidence Map
44	
45	为每个 contribution 建立 claim→evidence 映射表：
46	
47	| Contribution | Claim | Evidence | Table/Figure |
48	|-------------|-------|----------|-------------|
49	| C1: 方法 X 在 Y 上 SOTA | 比所有 baseline 高 ≥2% | 5-seed 平均，p<0.05 | Table 1 |
50	| C2: 消融证明 Z 是关键 | 去掉 Z 后掉 >5% | 消融实验 | Table 2 |
51	| C3: 计算效率 | 比 baseline 快 3× | FLOPs + wall-clock | Figure 3 |
52	
53	**没有直接证据支撑的 claim 必须删除或降级为 discussion。**
54	
55	### 2.3 章节起草顺序
56	
57	```
58	1. Introduction + Experiments（先确定 claim 和 evidence）
59	2. Method（评估问题稳定后再写细节）
60	3. Related Work
61	4. Abstract + Title（核心 claim 定型后最后写）
62	```
63	
64	### 2.4 Quality Gates
65	
66	投稿前必须通过：
67	- [ ] 前两段出现显式 novelty 声明
68	- [ ] 每个 contribution 有可验证的 evidence
69	- [ ] Abstract / Intro / Conclusion 的 claim 一致
70	- [ ] Limitations 真实且技术性诚实
71	- [ ] 审稿人两分钟内能识别 delta
72

75	## 3. 引用防幻觉（CRITICAL）
76	
77	**AI 生成引用有 ~40% 错误率。绝对禁止凭记忆写 BibTeX。**
78	
79	### 3.1 黄金法则
80	
81	```
82	IF 无法程序化获取引用:
83	    → 标记 [CITATION NEEDED] 或 \cite{PLACEHOLDER_verify}
84	    → 明确告知用户
85	    → 绝不编造看似合理的引用
86	```
87	
88	### 3.2 五步验证流程
89	
90	```
91	1. SEARCH  → Semantic Scholar API 搜索关键词
92	2. VERIFY  → 至少 2 个来源确认论文存在（S2 + arXiv/CrossRef）
93	3. RETRIEVE → 通过 DOI 获取 BibTeX（程序化，非记忆）
94	4. CHECK   → 确认你引用的 claim 确实出自该论文
95	5. ADD     → 加入 .bib 文件
96	```
97	
98	### 3.3 API 速查
99	
100	| API | 用途 | 限制 |
101	|-----|------|------|
102	| **Semantic Scholar** | ML/AI 论文搜索 | 1 RPS (免费) |
103	| **CrossRef** | DOI → BibTeX | 需 mailto 头 |
104	| **arXiv** | 预印本搜索 | 3s 间隔 |
105	
106	```python
107	# DOI → BibTeX（最可靠的方式）
108	import requests
109	def doi_to_bibtex(doi: str) -> str:
110	    r = requests.get(f"https://doi.org/{doi}",
111	                     headers={"Accept": "application/x-bibtex"})
112	    r.raise_for_status()
113	    return r.text
114	
115	# Semantic Scholar 搜索
116	from semanticscholar import SemanticScholar
117	sch = SemanticScholar()
118	results = sch.search_paper("attention mechanism transformers", limit=5)
119	for p in results:
120	    print(f"{p.title} | DOI: {p.externalIds.get('DOI', 'N/A')}")
121	```
122	
123	### 3.4 引用处理规则
124	
125	| 情况 | 处理 |
126	|------|------|
127	| 找到论文 + DOI + BibTeX | 直接用 |
128	| 找到论文，无 DOI | 用 arXiv BibTeX |
129	| 论文存在但无法获取 BibTeX | 标记 placeholder，告知用户 |
130	| 不确定论文是否存在 | 标记 `[CITATION NEEDED]`，告知用户 |
131	| "我觉得有篇关于 X 的论文" | **绝不引用** — 先搜索或标记 |

135	## 4. 顶会模板速查
136	
137	### 4.1 ML/AI 会议
138	
139	| 会议 | 页数限制 | 主文件 | 样式文件 | 必须项 |
140	|------|---------|--------|---------|--------|
141	| **NeurIPS** | 9 页 | `main.tex` | `neurips.sty` | Paper Checklist |
142	| **ICML** | 8 页 (+1 camera-ready) | `example_paper.tex` | `icml2026.sty` | Broader Impact |
143	| **ICLR** | 9 页 (+1) | `iclr_conference.tex` | `iclr_conference.sty` | LLM 使用声明 |
144	| **ACL/EMNLP** | 8 页 (long) | `acl_latex.tex` | `acl.sty` | Limitations 必须 |
145	| **AAAI** | 7 页 (+1) | `aaai_template.tex` | `aaai.sty` | 严格样式 |
146	| **COLM** | 9 页 (+1) | `colm_conference.tex` | `colm_conference.sty` | 语言模型聚焦 |
147	
148	### 4.2 系统会议
149	
150	| 会议 | 页数限制 | 模板类型 | 关键要求 |
151	|------|---------|---------|---------|
152	| **OSDI** | 12 页 (+2) | USENIX `usenix.sty` | Research / Operational 双 track |
153	| **NSDI** | 12 页 | USENIX | Introduction 预筛 |
154	| **ASPLOS** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 前 2 页快速评审 |
155	| **SOSP** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 可选 Artifact Evaluation |
156	
157	### 4.3 模板使用原则
158	
159	```bash
160	# 1. 复制整个模板目录（不要只拷 .tex）
161	cp -r templates/neurips2025/ ~/papers/my-paper/
162	
163	# 2. 先编译未修改的模板，确认能跑通
164	latexmk -pdf main.tex
165	
166	# 3. 逐章替换内容，频繁编译
167	```
168	
169	**禁止事项：**
170	- 不要修改 `.sty` 文件
171	- 不要在会议模板间复制 `\usepackage` 行
172	- 不要只复制 `.tex` 而不带 `.sty/.bst`

176	## 5. 写作规范
177	
178	### 5.1 时间分配（Neel Nanda）
179	
180	花**大致相等**的时间在：
181	1. Abstract
182	2. Introduction
183	3. 图表
184	4. **其余所有内容加起来**
185	
186	审稿人读论文的顺序：标题 → 摘要 → 引言 → 图表 → 也许正文。
187	
188	### 5.2 Abstract 五句法（Sebastian Farquhar）
189	
190	```
191	1. 你做了什么（"We introduce/prove/demonstrate..."）
192	2. 为什么这很难且重要
193	3. 怎么做的（含专业关键词以便检索）
194	4. 有什么证据
195	5. 最惊人的数字/结果
196	```
197	
198	删除一切泛泛的开头：~~"Large language models have achieved remarkable success..."~~
199	
200	### 5.3 句子级清晰度（Gopen & Swan）
201	
202	| 原则 | 规则 |
203	|------|------|
204	| 主谓紧邻 | 不要在主语和动词之间插入长从句 |
205	| 重点在句尾 | 把关键数字/结论放在句末 |
206	| 旧信息在前 | 先放读者已知的内容，再引入新概念 |
207	| 动词表达动作 | "We analyzed" 而非 "We performed an analysis" |
208	
209	### 5.4 常见修改
210	
211	| 问题 | 修复 |
212	|------|------|
213	| Abstract 太泛 | 删第一句（如果它能放在任何 ML 论文前面） |
214	| Introduction 超 1.5 页 | 背景挪到 Related Work |
215	| 实验没有显式 claim | 每个实验前加 "This tests whether..." |
216	| 缺统计显著性 | 加 error bars + 运行次数 + 计算方法 |
217

220	## 6. 投稿工程链
221	
222	### 6.1 构建
223	
224	```bash
225	# 推荐：latexmk 一键构建
226	latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex
227	
228	# 手动：需要多次编译
229	pdflatex main.tex && bibtex main && pdflatex main.tex && pdflatex main.tex
230	```
231	
232	### 6.2 Lint + 格式化
233	
234	```bash
235	# Lint: 检查常见 LaTeX 问题
236	chktex main.tex
237	
238	# 格式化: 减少 diff 噪声
239	latexindent -w main.tex
240	```
241	
242	### 6.3 图表格式
243	
244	| 类型 | 格式 | 说明 |
245	|------|------|------|
246	| 矢量图（plot、diagram） | PDF | matplotlib: `plt.savefig('fig.pdf')` |
247	| 照片/heatmap | PNG 600dpi 或 TIFF | 栅格图 |
248	| 表格 | `booktabs` 包 | `\toprule/\midrule/\bottomrule` |
249	
250	```latex
251	\usepackage{booktabs}
252	\begin{tabular}{lcc}
253	\toprule
254	Method & Accuracy $\uparrow$ & Latency $\downarrow$ \\
255	\midrule
256	Baseline & 85.2 & 45ms \\
257	\textbf{Ours} & \textbf{92.1} & 38ms \\
258	\bottomrule
259	\end{tabular}
260	```
261	
262	**图表规范：**
263	- 用色盲友好色板（Okabe-Ito 或 Paul Tol）
264	- 图内不放标题（用 caption）
265	- Caption 独立可理解（不依赖正文）
266	- 最佳值加粗，标注方向符号（↑ 越高越好，↓ 越低越好）
267	
268	### 6.4 投稿打包
269	
270	```bash
271	# 清理辅助文件
272	latexmk -c
273	
274	# 打包投稿
275	zip -r submission.zip main.tex *.sty *.bst *.bib figures/ --exclude='*.aux' --exclude='*.log'
276	```
277	
278	### 6.5 常见失败点
279	
280	| 问题 | 解决 |
281	|------|------|
282	| 图片格式混用导致编译失败 | 统一用 PDF |
283	| 字体未嵌入 | `pdffonts output.pdf` 检查 |
284	| Overfull box 过多 | 关键位置手动调行 |
285	| 引用缺字段 | 检查 DOI/年份/期刊名 |
286	| 超页数 | 用 `\vspace{-Xpt}` 微调，或精简内容 |

# LaTeX 论文写作全流程

ML/AI 顶会论文从草稿到投稿的完整指南。整合 Orchestra Research、VibeSkills、claim2evidence 三方最佳实践。

---

## 1. 工作模式

开始前选择模式：

| 模式 | 说明 | 适用 |
|------|------|------|
| **Build** | 从实验笔记/结果/代码生成论文 | 新稿 |
| **Improve** | 改写已有章节，强化论证 | 修改稿 |
| **Audit** | 输出风险列表 + 缺失证据 + 修复建议 | 投前检查 |

---

## 2. Claim-Evidence 方法论

**核心原则：论文是一个有中心贡献的故事，不是实验的堆砌。**

### 2.1 一句话贡献

在写任何内容之前，必须能用一句话说清贡献。如果不能，说明还没准备好写论文。

### 2.2 Claim-Evidence Map

为每个 contribution 建立 claim→evidence 映射表：

| Contribution | Claim | Evidence | Table/Figure |
|-------------|-------|----------|-------------|
| C1: 方法 X 在 Y 上 SOTA | 比所有 baseline 高 ≥2% | 5-seed 平均，p<0.05 | Table 1 |
| C2: 消融证明 Z 是关键 | 去掉 Z 后掉 >5% | 消融实验 | Table 2 |
| C3: 计算效率 | 比 baseline 快 3× | FLOPs + wall-clock | Figure 3 |

**没有直接证据支撑的 claim 必须删除或降级为 discussion。**

### 2.3 章节起草顺序

```
1. Introduction + Experiments（先确定 claim 和 evidence）
2. Method（评估问题稳定后再写细节）
3. Related Work
4. Abstract + Title（核心 claim 定型后最后写）
```

### 2.4 Quality Gates

投稿前必须通过：
- [ ] 前两段出现显式 novelty 声明
- [ ] 每个 contribution 有可验证的 evidence
- [ ] Abstract / Intro / Conclusion 的 claim 一致
- [ ] Limitations 真实且技术性诚实
- [ ] 审稿人两分钟内能识别 delta

---

## 3. 引用防幻觉（CRITICAL）

**AI 生成引用有 ~40% 错误率。绝对禁止凭记忆写 BibTeX。**

### 3.1 黄金法则

```
IF 无法程序化获取引用:
    → 标记 [CITATION NEEDED] 或 \cite{PLACEHOLDER_verify}
    → 明确告知用户
    → 绝不编造看似合理的引用
```

### 3.2 五步验证流程

```
1. SEARCH  → Semantic Scholar API 搜索关键词
2. VERIFY  → 至少 2 个来源确认论文存在（S2 + arXiv/CrossRef）
3. RETRIEVE → 通过 DOI 获取 BibTeX（程序化，非记忆）
4. CHECK   → 确认你引用的 claim 确实出自该论文
5. ADD     → 加入 .bib 文件
```

### 3.3 API 速查

| API | 用途 | 限制 |
|-----|------|------|
| **Semantic Scholar** | ML/AI 论文搜索 | 1 RPS (免费) |
| **CrossRef** | DOI → BibTeX | 需 mailto 头 |
| **arXiv** | 预印本搜索 | 3s 间隔 |

```python
# DOI → BibTeX（最可靠的方式）
import requests
def doi_to_bibtex(doi: str) -> str:
    r = requests.get(f"https://doi.org/{doi}",
                     headers={"Accept": "application/x-bibtex"})
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.text

# Semantic Scholar 搜索
from semanticscholar import SemanticScholar
sch = SemanticScholar()
results = sch.search_paper("attention mechanism transformers", limit=5)
for p in results:
    print(f"{p.title} | DOI: {p.externalIds.get('DOI', 'N/A')}")
```

### 3.4 引用处理规则

| 情况 | 处理 |
|------|------|
| 找到论文 + DOI + BibTeX | 直接用 |
| 找到论文，无 DOI | 用 arXiv BibTeX |
| 论文存在但无法获取 BibTeX | 标记 placeholder，告知用户 |
| 不确定论文是否存在 | 标记 `[CITATION NEEDED]`，告知用户 |
| "我觉得有篇关于 X 的论文" | **绝不引用** — 先搜索或标记 |

| **OSDI** | 12 页 (+2) | USENIX `usenix.sty` | Research / Operational 双 track |

| **ASPLOS** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 前 2 页快速评审 |
| **SOSP** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 可选 Artifact Evaluation |

### 4.3 模板使用原则

```bash
# 1. 复制整个模板目录（不要只拷 .tex）
cp -r templates/neurips2025/ ~/papers/my-paper/

# 2. 先编译未修改的模板，确认能跑通
latexmk -pdf main.tex

# 3. 逐章替换内容，频繁编译
```

**禁止事项：**
- 不要修改 `.sty` 文件
- 不要在会议模板间复制 `\usepackage` 行
- 不要只复制 `.tex` 而不带 `.sty/.bst`

---

## 5. 写作规范

### 5.1 时间分配（Neel Nanda）

花**大致相等**的时间在：
1. Abstract
2. Introduction
3. 图表
4. **其余所有内容加起来**

审稿人读论文的顺序：标题 → 摘要 → 引言 → 图表 → 也许正文。

### 5.2 Abstract 五句法（Sebastian Farquhar）

```
1. 你做了什么（"We introduce/prove/demonstrate..."）
2. 为什么这很难且重要
3. 怎么做的（含专业关键词以便检索）
4. 有什么证据
5. 最惊人的数字/结果
```

删除一切泛泛的开头：~~"Large language models have achieved remarkable success..."~~

### 5.3 句子级清晰度（Gopen & Swan）

| 原则 | 规则 |
|------|------|
| 主谓紧邻 | 不要在主语和动词之间插入长从句 |
| 重点在句尾 | 把关键数字/结论放在句末 |
| 旧信息在前 | 先放读者已知的内容，再引入新概念 |
| 动词表达动作 | "We analyzed" 而非 "We performed an analysis" |

### 5.4 常见修改

| 问题 | 修复 |
|------|------|
| Abstract 太泛 | 删第一句（如果它能放在任何 ML 论文前面） |
| Introduction 超 1.5 页 | 背景挪到 Related Work |
| 实验没有显式 claim | 每个实验前加 "This tests whether..." |
| 缺统计显著性 | 加 error bars + 运行次数 + 计算方法 |

---

## 6. 投稿工程链

### 6.1 构建

```bash
# 推荐：latexmk 一键构建
latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex

# 手动：需要多次编译
pdflatex main.tex && bibtex main && pdflatex main.tex && pdflatex main.tex
```

### 6.2 Lint + 格式化

```bash
# Lint: 检查常见 LaTeX 问题
chktex main.tex

# 格式化: 减少 diff 噪声
latexindent -w main.tex
```

### 6.3 图表格式

| 类型 | 格式 | 说明 |
|------|------|------|
| 矢量图（plot、diagram） | PDF | matplotlib: `plt.savefig('fig.pdf')` |
| 照片/heatmap | PNG 600dpi 或 TIFF | 栅格图 |
| 表格 | `booktabs` 包 | `\toprule/\midrule/\bottomrule` |

```latex
\usepackage{booktabs}
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
Method & Accuracy $\uparrow$ & Latency $\downarrow$ \\
\midrule
Baseline & 85.2 & 45ms \\
\textbf{Ours} & \textbf{92.1} & 38ms \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
```

**图表规范：**
- 用色盲友好色板（Okabe-Ito 或 Paul Tol）
- 图内不放标题（用 caption）
- Caption 独立可理解（不依赖正文）
- 最佳值加粗，标注方向符号（↑ 越高越好，↓ 越低越好）

### 6.4 投稿打包

```bash
# 清理辅助文件
latexmk -c

# 打包投稿
zip -r submission.zip main.tex *.sty *.bst *.bib figures/ --exclude='*.aux' --exclude='*.log'
```

### 6.5 常见失败点

| 问题 | 解决 |
|------|------|
| 图片格式混用导致编译失败 | 统一用 PDF |
| 字体未嵌入 | `pdffonts output.pdf` 检查 |
| Overfull box 过多 | 关键位置手动调行 |
| 引用缺字段 | 检查 DOI/年份/期刊名 |
| 超页数 | 用 `\vspace{-Xpt}` 微调，或精简内容 |

---

## 7. 会议转投

当论文被拒或转投其他会议时：

### 7.1 ML/AI 会议间转换

| 转换 | 页数变化 | 关键调整 |
|------|---------|---------|
| NeurIPS → ICML | 9→8 | 删 1 页，加 Broader Impact |
| ICML → ICLR | 8→9 | 可扩展实验 + LLM 声明 |
| NeurIPS → ACL | 9→8 | 按 NLP 惯例重组 + Limitations |
| ICLR → AAAI | 9→7 | 大幅精简，严格样式 |

### 7.2 转投原则

1. **永远用目标模板重新开始** — 复制目标模板，迁移内容，不要合并 preamble
2. **只迁移正文内容** — 不复制 `\usepackage`、header/footer 命令
3. **根据审稿意见改进** — 但不要在新稿中提及旧投稿（双盲）
4. **检查目标会议特殊要求** — checklist、ethics statement、LLM 声明等

---

## 8. 投前清单

### 通用清单

- [ ] Abstract/Intro/Conclusion 的 claim 一致
- [ ] 每个 contribution 有对应 evidence
- [ ] 所有引用已程序化验证（无幻觉引用）
- [ ] Error bars + 运行次数 + 统计方法
- [ ] Limitations 章节存在且诚实
- [ ] 匿名化（双盲审稿）
- [ ] 符合页数限制
- [ ] 所有图表有自包含 caption
- [ ] `.bib` 中无缺失字段
- [ ] PDF 编译无 warning

### 会议特定

| 会议 | 额外要求 |
|------|---------|
| NeurIPS | 16 项 Paper Checklist（附录，不计页数） |
| ICML | Broader Impact Statement |
| ICLR | LLM 使用声明 |
| ACL/EMNLP | Limitations 章节（必须），Ethics Statement |
| AAAI | 严格样式文件合规 |

content.content:
1	\section{Experiments}
2	\label{sec:experiments}
3	
4	\subsection{Experimental Setup}
5	\label{sec:setup}
6	
7	\paragraph{Datasets.}
8	We evaluate on three English IE benchmarks spanning a difficulty gradient.
9	\textbf{SciERC} \cite{luan2018scierc} contains 551 test instances from scientific abstracts annotated for joint NER (6 entity types) and RE (7 relation types), representing a complex schema with overlapping structures.
10	\textbf{CoNLL-2003} \cite{tjongkimsang2003conll} provides 3{,}453 test sentences from newswire with 4 entity types, serving as a high-accuracy benchmark where models achieve ${>}$91\% micro F1.
11	\textbf{WNUT-17} \cite{derczynski2017wnut} consists of 1{,}287 test instances from social media with emerging entities, used to probe method boundaries where model capability is insufficient.
12	This gradient---from near-solved (CoNLL) through challenging (SciERC) to infeasible (WNUT-17)---enables systematic characterization of how signal effectiveness varies with task difficulty (\S\ref{sec:complexity_robustness}).
13	
14	\paragraph{Models.}
15	Our primary model is \textbf{Qwen3-8B}, fine-tuned with LoRA ($r{=}32$) separately per dataset.
16	For cross-model validation, we evaluate \textbf{LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct} to assess whether structural confidence signals transfer across architectures and training regimes.
17	
18	\paragraph{Sampling and Evaluation.}
19	For each test instance, we draw $N$ independent samples at temperature $T{=}1.0$, with $T{=}0.7$ for robustness analysis.
20	We use $N{=}8$ for both SciERC and CoNLL in the primary evaluation, and $N{=}16$ for SciERC scaling experiments.
21	Quality estimation is measured along two axes: \textit{rank correlation} with instance-level F1 via Spearman $\rho$ and Kendall $\tau$, and \textit{binary discrimination} via AUROC (instances above vs.\ below median F1).
22	Downstream utility is assessed through \textbf{best-of-$N$ selection F1}: the F1 obtained when each signal selects one sample per instance.
23	Instance-level F1 uses exact span matching for NER and head-tail-label matching for RE, where a relation is correct only when both argument entities and the relation label match the gold annotation.
24	The greedy decoding baseline ($T{=}0$, $N{=}1$) establishes performance without test-time scaling.
25	
26	\paragraph{Confidence Signals.}
27	We compare five signals from three families (detailed in \S\ref{sec:signals}).
28	\textit{Structural} signals operate on extracted entity/relation sets: \textbf{Voting Confidence} aggregates per-extraction frequency across samples, and \textbf{Soft Jaccard (SJ)} measures pairwise set similarity \cite{jaccard1901distribution}.
29	\textit{Surface} signals operate on string representations: \textbf{Fleiss' $\kappa$ (FK)} quantifies inter-sample agreement treating samples as independent annotators \cite{fleiss1971agreement}, and \textbf{Exact Match (EM)} computes the fraction of identical sample pairs.
30	The \textit{model-internal} signal is \textbf{log-probability (logprob)}, the mean token-level log-likelihood.
31	
32	\paragraph{Implementation.}
33	Inference uses vLLM with XGrammar constrained decoding \cite{willard2023guided} to enforce valid JSON output structure.
34	A span realignment post-processing step corrects character-level offset mismatches between generated and gold annotation spans.

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

\subsection{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:setup}

\paragraph{Datasets.}
We evaluate on three English IE benchmarks spanning a difficulty gradient.
\textbf{SciERC} \cite{luan2018scierc} contains 551 test instances from scientific abstracts annotated for joint NER (6 entity types) and RE (7 relation types), representing a complex schema with overlapping structures.
\textbf{CoNLL-2003} \cite{tjongkimsang2003conll} provides 3{,}453 test sentences from newswire with 4 entity types, serving as a high-accuracy benchmark where models achieve ${>}$91\% micro F1.
\textbf{WNUT-17} \cite{derczynski2017wnut} consists of 1{,}287 test instances from social media with emerging entities, used to probe method boundaries where model capability is insufficient.
This gradient---from near-solved (CoNLL) through challenging (SciERC) to infeasible (WNUT-17)---enables systematic characterization of how signal effectiveness varies with task difficulty (\S\ref{sec:complexity_robustness}).

\paragraph{Models.}
Our primary model is \textbf{Qwen3-8B}, fine-tuned with LoRA ($r{=}32$) separately per dataset.
For cross-model validation, we evaluate \textbf{LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct} to assess whether structural confidence signals transfer across architectures and training regimes.

\paragraph{Sampling and Evaluation.}
For each test instance, we draw $N$ independent samples at temperature $T{=}1.0$, with $T{=}0.7$ for robustness analysis.
We use $N{=}8$ for both SciERC and CoNLL in the primary evaluation, and $N{=}16$ for SciERC scaling experiments.
Quality estimation is measured along two axes: \textit{rank correlation} with instance-level F1 via Spearman $\rho$ and Kendall $\tau$, and \textit{binary discrimination} via AUROC (instances above vs.\ below median F1).
Downstream utility is assessed through \textbf{best-of-$N$ selection F1}: the F1 obtained when each signal selects one sample per instance.
Instance-level F1 uses exact span matching for NER and head-tail-label matching for RE, where a relation is correct only when both argument entities and the relation label match the gold annotation.
The greedy decoding baseline ($T{=}0$, $N{=}1$) establishes performance without test-time scaling.

\paragraph{Confidence Signals.}
We compare five signals from three families (detailed in \S\ref{sec:signals}).
\textit{Structural} signals operate on extracted entity/relation sets: \textbf{Voting Confidence} aggregates per-extraction frequency across samples, and \textbf{Soft Jaccard (SJ)} measures pairwise set similarity \cite{jaccard1901distribution}.
\textit{Surface} signals operate on string representations: \textbf{Fleiss' $\kappa$ (FK)} quantifies inter-sample agreement treating samples as independent annotators \cite{fleiss1971agreement}, and \textbf{Exact Match (EM)} computes the fraction of identical sample pairs.
The \textit{model-internal} signal is \textbf{log-probability (logprob)}, the mean token-level log-likelihood.

\paragraph{Implementation.}
Inference uses vLLM with XGrammar constrained decoding \cite{willard2023guided} to enforce valid JSON output structure.
A span realignment post-processing step corrects character-level offset mismatches between generated and gold annotation spans.
All confidence signals are computed from the $N$ samples without access to gold labels.

%% ============================================================
\subsection{Quality Estimation Results}
\label{sec:qe_results}

\begin{table*}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Quality estimation across tasks and models (Spearman $\rho$ and AUROC). All results use $N{=}8$ samples at $T{=}1.0$. Best value per column in \textbf{bold}. SciERC evaluates joint NER (6 types) and RE (7 types); CoNLL evaluates NER (4 types) with two model families.}
\label{tab:quality_estimation}
\begin{tabular}{ll cc cc cc cc}
\toprule
& & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{SciERC NER}} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{SciERC RE}} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{CoNLL (Qwen)}} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{CoNLL (LLaMA)}} \\
\cmidrule(lr){3-4} \cmidrule(lr){5-6} \cmidrule(lr){7-8} \cmidrule(lr){9-10}
Signal & Family & $\rho$ & AUC & $\rho$ & AUC & $\rho$ & AUC & $\rho$ & AUC \\
\midrule
Voting Conf. & Structural & \textbf{.502} & \textbf{.728} & \textbf{.422} & \textbf{.716} & .424 & .789 & .426 & .709 \\
Soft Jaccard  & Structural & .357 & .666 & .211 & .582 & .436 & .801 & \textbf{.431} & .704 \\
Fleiss' $\kappa$ & Surface & .265 & .624 & .253 & .631 & .400 & .774 & .428 & .703 \\
Exact Match  & Surface    & .257 & .623 & .100 & .504 & \textbf{.451} & \textbf{.816} & \textbf{.431} & .705 \\
Log-prob     & Model      & .140 & .559 & .247 & .635 & .316 & .753 & .307 & \textbf{.761} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table*}

Table~\ref{tab:quality_estimation} presents rank correlation ($\rho$) and AUROC for five confidence signals across tasks and models.

\paragraph{Structural signals dominate on complex schemas.}
On SciERC NER, Voting Confidence achieves $\rho{=}0.502$, substantially outperforming the second-best signal, SJ ($\rho{=}0.357$), and all remaining signals ($\rho{\leq}0.265$).
Voting's advantage reflects its extraction-level granularity: it rewards entities that appear consistently while penalizing hallucinated or missed ones, whereas SJ compares entire sets and is sensitive to both overlap and total extraction count.
The structural advantage persists on RE, where Voting ($\rho{=}0.422$) again leads.
However, all signals weaken on RE: 44\% of instances receive zero F1, creating a floor effect that compresses the discriminable range.
Notably, FK ($\rho{=}0.253$) exceeds SJ ($\rho{=}0.211$) on RE---a reversal from NER that shows no single structural signal dominates across both tasks.

\paragraph{Signal rankings shift with task difficulty.}
On CoNLL NER, where greedy decoding achieves ${>}$91\% micro F1, the signal landscape changes substantially.
Exact Match leads with $\rho{=}0.451$ and AUROC${=}0.816$, surpassing SJ ($\rho{=}0.436$) and Voting ($\rho{=}0.424$).
When most samples are near-correct, binary agreement captures the remaining variance more efficiently than set-level similarity.
This reversal---EM${>}$SJ on easy tasks vs.\ SJ${>}$EM on hard tasks---demonstrates that optimal signal choice depends on intrinsic task difficulty.

\paragraph{Cross-model stability.}
Comparing Qwen and LLaMA on CoNLL, SJ shows remarkable stability: $\rho{=}0.436$ (Qwen) vs.\ $\rho{=}0.431$ (LLaMA), a gap of only 0.005.
This model-agnostic property is expected for structural signals that operate on outputs rather than internal model states, and provides the strongest evidence that SJ generalizes across architectures.
The SJ--FK gap also narrows with schema simplification: $\Delta\rho{=}0.092$ on SciERC NER (6 entity types) vs.\ $\Delta\rho{=}0.003$ on CoNLL with LLaMA (4 types), suggesting that set-level structure contributes less when the type inventory is small.

81	\paragraph{The logprob paradox.}
82	Log-probability reveals a dissociation between ranking and classification.
83	On CoNLL with LLaMA, it achieves the highest AUROC (0.761) yet the lowest $\rho$ (0.307) among all signals.
84	This pattern indicates that logprob assigns well-separated scores to easy vs.\ hard instances (strong binary discrimination) but provides little resolution within each group (weak ranking), making it better suited for binary filtering than continuous quality estimation.
85	We return to this distinction in \S\ref{sec:complexity_robustness} and visualize it in Figure~\ref{fig:signal_heatmap}.
86	
87	\paragraph{Oracle headroom and practical ceilings.}
88	On CoNLL, oracle best-of-$N$ selection yields only +4.2~pp (Qwen) and +1.8~pp (LLaMA) over greedy.
89	When the model already operates near its performance ceiling, confidence signals serve as \textit{reliability assurance}---confirming that outputs are trustworthy---rather than enabling selective prediction gains.
90	We therefore focus selection analysis (\S\ref{sec:selection_gap}) on SciERC, where oracle headroom exceeds 16~pp.
91	
92	%% ============================================================
93	\subsection{The Correlation-Selection Gap}
94	\label{sec:selection_gap}
95	
96	\begin{table}[t]
97	\centering
98	\small
99	\caption{Best-of-$N$ selection F1 on SciERC ($N{=}8$, $T{=}1.0$). Best non-oracle result per column in \textbf{bold}. EM produces binary agreement without sample ranking.}
100	\label{tab:selection}
101	\begin{tabular}{lcc}
102	\toprule
103	Method & NER F1 & RE F1 \\
104	\midrule
105	Oracle & 0.769 & 0.561 \\
106	\midrule
107	Log-prob           & 0.609 & \textbf{0.397} \\
108	Ensemble (SJ+Vot.) & 0.604 & 0.367 \\
109	Soft Jaccard       & 0.604 & 0.368 \\
110	Voting             & 0.596 & 0.338 \\
111	Exact Match        & ---   & ---   \\
112	\midrule
113	Greedy ($T{=}0$)   & \textbf{0.609} & 0.374 \\
114	Random             & 0.580 & 0.338 \\
115	\bottomrule
116	\end{tabular}
117	\end{table}
118	
119	Despite strong quality estimation, confidence signals yield limited gains when used for best-of-$N$ selection.
120	Table~\ref{tab:selection} compares selection F1 on SciERC ($N{=}8$).
121	
122	\paragraph{NER: no signal surpasses greedy.}
123	The oracle upper bound (0.769) reveals 16.0~pp of headroom above greedy (0.609).
124	Yet no confidence signal closes this gap.
125	Log-probability (0.609) merely ties greedy; the best quality estimator, Voting ($\rho{=}0.502$), selects to only 0.596, \textit{below} greedy.
126	An ensemble of SJ and Voting (AUROC${=}0.735$) also fails, achieving 0.604.
127	The greedy--logprob tie is revealing: log-probability selects the sample with highest model confidence, which on average matches the deterministic greedy output, implying that the $N$ samples cluster at a similar quality level with insufficient variance for any signal to exploit.
128	The Random baseline (0.580) confirms that not all samples are equal---uniform selection loses 2.9~pp vs.\ greedy---but the discriminative structure captured by confidence signals adds no value beyond greedy's deterministic choice.
129	
130	\paragraph{RE: logprob uniquely succeeds.}
131	For RE, log-probability is the only signal to exceed greedy (0.397 vs.\ 0.374, +2.3~pp).
132	Structural signals trail or match greedy: SJ selects to 0.368 and Voting to 0.338.
133	The oracle gap of 18.7~pp (0.561 vs.\ 0.374) indicates substantially more per-instance variance than NER.
134	Log-probability's success here may stem from its per-token nature: unlike instance-level consistency signals, logprob evaluates each sample independently, enabling it to distinguish a particularly successful extraction from its peers even when all extractions share similar structural consistency.
135	
136	\paragraph{Quality estimation $\neq$ output selection.}
137	We attribute this gap (Figure~\ref{fig:selection_gap}) to a fundamental distinction: instance-level confidence signals predict \textit{which inputs} the model handles reliably, not \textit{which output} among $N$ candidates is best for a given input.
138	When per-sample variance is low relative to instance-level difficulty---as in NER, where the model often produces $N$ similar extractions---even perfect quality estimation cannot discriminate among near-identical candidates.
139	
140	\paragraph{Implications for test-time scaling.}
141	This correlation-selection gap has direct consequences for test-time scaling in IE \cite{brown2024monkeys, snell2024scaling}.
142	Scaling inference compute through repeated sampling assumes a selector can identify the best sample.
143	Our results show that for structured prediction, existing confidence signals serve as quality \textit{estimators}---useful for flagging unreliable predictions---but not as effective \textit{selectors}.
144	Closing this gap likely requires signals that capture per-sample rather than per-instance variation, such as trained verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers} or pairwise comparison models.
145	
146	%% ============================================================
147	\subsection{Task Complexity and Signal Robustness}
148	\label{sec:complexity_robustness}
149	
150	\paragraph{Task difficulty as a boundary condition.}
151	Signal effectiveness varies systematically with task difficulty.
152	On CoNLL (greedy micro F1${>}$0.91), EM leads all signals ($\rho{=}0.451$); on SciERC NER (micro F1$\,{\approx}\,$0.66), SJ overtakes EM ($\rho{=}0.357$ vs.\ 0.257); on SciERC RE, where 44\% of instances score zero F1, all signals converge to $\rho{\approx}0.25$.
153	The NER--RE difference is statistically confirmed: Fisher's $z$-test on $\rho_\text{SJ}$ yields $z{=}2.31$, $p{=}0.021$.
154	
155	\paragraph{Per-relation diagnostic.}
156	RE signal degradation is relation-specific.
157	\textsc{Feature-Of} has near-zero correlation ($\rho{=}0.004$), while \textsc{Hyponym-Of} achieves $\rho{=}0.646$.
158	The primary bottleneck is entity span errors, which account for 55.5\% of RE false negatives---a prerequisite failure that consistency signals cannot detect, as they measure agreement among equally incorrect extractions.

210	
211	\paragraph{Evaluation circularity.}
212	Leave-one-out SJ (LOO-SJ), which excludes the target sample when computing confidence, yields $\Delta\rho{=}{-}0.014$ relative to standard SJ, with a maximum per-instance $\Delta\rho$ of $3.1{\times}10^{-4}$.
213	Evaluation circularity is negligible.
214	
215	\paragraph{Conditional filtering reveals signal divergence.}
216	Filtering to non-zero F1 instances improves SJ correlations: NER $\rho{=}0.412$ (from 0.357), RE $\rho{=}0.368$ at $N{=}8$.
217	At $N{=}16$, signal families diverge sharply on conditional RE: SJ maintains $\rho{=}0.308$, while logprob drops to $\rho{=}{-}0.026$---effectively zero---showing that logprob's apparent RE utility at $N{=}8$ does not generalize to larger sample sets.
218	For applications that can first filter out catastrophic failures, SJ's effective ranking approaches $\rho{\approx}0.4$ on both NER and RE, a regime where quality-aware aggregation can provide meaningful benefit.
219	
220	\paragraph{Binary filtering vs.\ continuous ranking.}
221	The logprob paradox observed in Table~\ref{tab:quality_estimation}---highest AUROC (0.761) but lowest $\rho$ (0.307) on CoNLL with LLaMA---reflects a fundamental distinction in how signals encode quality information.
222	Log-probability provides coarse separation between reliable and unreliable instances (suited for accept/reject thresholds), while structural signals like SJ and Voting provide finer-grained ranking (suited for prioritization and quality-aware aggregation).
223	Figure~\ref{fig:reliability} visualizes this complementarity across the difficulty spectrum.
224	Practitioners should select signal type based on the downstream application: binary filtering favors logprob; ranking-dependent decisions favor structural consistency.

\paragraph{Capability stratification.}
SJ effectiveness scales with structural complexity: on SciERC instances with 6+ entities, $\rho{=}0.547$, compared to $\rho{=}0.415$ for 1--2 entities.
The SJ advantage over logprob remains stable across sentence-length quartiles ($\Delta\rho{\approx}0.08$--$0.20$), and three independent complexity proxies (entity count, sentence length, relation density) show weak mutual correlation ($|r|{<}0.15$), indicating a genuinely multi-dimensional benefit rather than a single confound.

\paragraph{Method boundary: WNUT-17.}
WNUT-17 establishes where the approach breaks down.
SJ achieves $\rho{=}0.062$ ($p{=}0.106$, not statistically significant), with 54\% of instances at zero F1.
Log-probability shows a strong \textit{negative} correlation ($\rho{=}{-}0.411$): the model is confidently wrong on novel entities, a calibration failure that no post-hoc consistency signal can remedy.
This is a boundary of the method, not a limitation of the datasets.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Signal robustness across temperature and sample size on SciERC (Spearman $\rho$). $^\dagger$Mean over 3 seeds ($\sigma{=}0.025$; individual: 0.428, 0.424, 0.384).}
\label{tab:robustness}
\begin{tabular}{llcc}
\toprule
& & NER $\rho$ & RE $\rho$ \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{4}{l}{\textit{Temperature} ($N{=}8$)} \\
\quad SJ & $T{=}0.7$ & 0.388 & 0.234 \\
\quad SJ & $T{=}1.0$ & 0.357 & 0.211 \\
\quad FK & $T{=}0.7$ & 0.321 & 0.184 \\
\quad FK & $T{=}1.0$ & 0.265 & 0.253 \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{4}{l}{\textit{Sample size} ($T{=}1.0$)} \\
\quad SJ & $N{=}8$  & 0.357 & 0.211 \\
\quad SJ & $N{=}16$ & 0.412$^\dagger$ & 0.281 \\
\quad FK & $N{=}8$  & 0.265 & 0.253 \\
\quad FK & $N{=}16$ & 0.280 & 0.279 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Robustness analysis.}
Table~\ref{tab:robustness} reports signal stability across temperature and sample size on SciERC.
\textit{Temperature.}
SJ NER $\rho$ shifts from 0.388 ($T{=}0.7$) to 0.357 ($T{=}1.0$), a difference of 0.031 whose bootstrap confidence interval includes zero.
FK shows mixed behavior: NER $\rho$ drops by 0.056, while RE $\rho$ increases by 0.069, likely reflecting reduced diversity at lower temperature interacting differently across tasks.
Across all comparisons, the SJ--FK relative ordering is preserved at both temperatures on NER (0.388 vs.\ 0.321 at $T{=}0.7$; 0.357 vs.\ 0.265 at $T{=}1.0$), indicating a stable signal hierarchy despite numerically small temperature effects.

\textit{Sample size.}
Increasing from $N{=}8$ to $N{=}16$ yields meaningful gains for SJ on NER: $\rho$ improves from 0.357 to $0.412{\pm}0.025$ (three seeds: 0.428, 0.424, 0.384).
FK benefits less ($\rho{\approx}0.280$ at $N{=}16$ vs.\ 0.265 at $N{=}8$).
For RE at $N{=}16$, SJ ($\rho{=}0.281$), FK ($\rho{=}0.279$), and logprob ($\rho{=}0.287$) all plateau at comparable levels, suggesting that compound entity-then-relation errors impose a ceiling that additional samples cannot overcome.

\paragraph{Cross-model transfer.}
LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct replicates the structural-over-surface ordering on SciERC NER (SJ $\rho{=}0.363$, FK $\rho{=}0.327$).
On CoNLL, the cross-model gap is minimal (Table~\ref{tab:quality_estimation}): SJ achieves $\rho{=}0.431$ (LLaMA) vs.\ 0.436 (Qwen), $\Delta{=}0.005$.
On conditional RE (non-zero F1 instances), SJ recovers to $\rho{=}0.405$ while FK drops to $\rho{=}0.259$, confirming that structural advantage is robust across both models and evaluation conditions.

\paragraph{Evaluation circularity.}
Leave-one-out SJ (LOO-SJ), which excludes the target sample when computing confidence, yields $\Delta\rho{=}{-}0.014$ relative to standard SJ, with a maximum per-instance $\Delta\rho$ of $3.1{\times}10^{-4}$.
Evaluation circularity is negligible.

\paragraph{Conditional filtering reveals signal divergence.}
Filtering to non-zero F1 instances improves SJ correlations: NER $\rho{=}0.412$ (from 0.357), RE $\rho{=}0.368$ at $N{=}8$.
At $N{=}16$, signal families diverge sharply on conditional RE: SJ maintains $\rho{=}0.308$, while logprob drops to $\rho{=}{-}0.026$---effectively zero---showing that logprob's apparent RE utility at $N{=}8$ does not generalize to larger sample sets.
For applications that can first filter out catastrophic failures, SJ's effective ranking approaches $\rho{\approx}0.4$ on both NER and RE, a regime where quality-aware aggregation can provide meaningful benefit.

\paragraph{Binary filtering vs.\ continuous ranking.}
The logprob paradox observed in Table~\ref{tab:quality_estimation}---highest AUROC (0.761) but lowest $\rho$ (0.307) on CoNLL with LLaMA---reflects a fundamental distinction in how signals encode quality information.
Log-probability provides coarse separation between reliable and unreliable instances (suited for accept/reject thresholds), while structural signals like SJ and Voting provide finer-grained ranking (suited for prioritization and quality-aware aggregation).
Figure~\ref{fig:reliability} visualizes this complementarity across the difficulty spectrum.
Practitioners should select signal type based on the downstream application: binary filtering favors logprob; ranking-dependent decisions favor structural consistency.

1	\section{Experiments}
2	\label{sec:experiments}
3	
4	\subsection{Experimental Setup}
5	\label{sec:setup}
6	
7	\paragraph{Datasets.}
8	We evaluate on three English IE benchmarks spanning a difficulty gradient.
9	\textbf{SciERC} \cite{luan2018scierc} contains 551 test instances from scientific abstracts annotated for joint NER (6 entity types) and RE (7 relation types), representing a complex schema with overlapping structures.
10	\textbf{CoNLL-2003} \cite{tjongkimsang2003conll} provides 3{,}453 test sentences from newswire with 4 entity types, serving as a high-accuracy benchmark where models achieve ${>}$91\% micro F1.
11	\textbf{WNUT-17} \cite{derczynski2017wnut} consists of 1{,}287 test instances from social media with emerging entities, used to probe method boundaries where model capability is insufficient.
12	This gradient---from near-solved (CoNLL) through challenging (SciERC) to infeasible (WNUT-17)---enables systematic characterization of how signal effectiveness varies with task difficulty (\S\ref{sec:complexity_robustness}).
13	
14	\paragraph{Models.}
15	Our primary model is \textbf{Qwen3-8B}, fine-tuned with LoRA ($r{=}32$) separately per dataset.
16	For cross-model validation, we evaluate \textbf{LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct} to assess whether structural confidence signals transfer across architectures and training regimes.
17	
18	\paragraph{Sampling and Evaluation.}
19	For each test instance, we draw $N$ independent samples at temperature $T{=}1.0$, with $T{=}0.7$ for robustness analysis.
20	We use $N{=}8$ for both SciERC and CoNLL in the primary evaluation, and $N{=}16$ for SciERC scaling experiments.
21	Quality estimation is measured along two axes: \textit{rank correlation} with instance-level F1 via Spearman $\rho$ and Kendall $\tau$, and \textit{binary discrimination} via AUROC (instances above vs.\ below median F1).
22	Downstream utility is assessed through \textbf{best-of-$N$ selection F1}: the F1 obtained when each signal selects one sample per instance.
23	Instance-level F1 uses exact span matching for NER and head-tail-label matching for RE, where a relation is correct only when both argument entities and the relation label match the gold annotation.
24	The greedy decoding baseline ($T{=}0$, $N{=}1$) establishes performance without test-time scaling.
25	
26	\paragraph{Confidence Signals.}
27	We compare five signals from three families (detailed in \S\ref{sec:signals}).
28	\textit{Structural} signals operate on extracted entity/relation sets: \textbf{Voting Confidence} aggregates per-extraction frequency across samples, and \textbf{Soft Jaccard (SJ)} measures pairwise set similarity \cite{jaccard1901distribution}.
29	\textit{Surface} signals operate on string representations: \textbf{Fleiss' $\kappa$ (FK)} quantifies inter-sample agreement treating samples as independent annotators \cite{fleiss1971agreement}, and \textbf{Exact Match (EM)} computes the fraction of identical sample pairs.
30	The \textit{model-internal} signal is \textbf{log-probability (logprob)}, the mean token-level log-likelihood.
31	
32	\paragraph{Implementation.}
33	Inference uses vLLM with XGrammar constrained decoding \cite{willard2023guided} to enforce valid JSON output structure.
34	A span realignment post-processing step corrects character-level offset mismatches between generated and gold annotation spans.
35	All confidence signals are computed from the $N$ samples without access to gold labels.
36	
37	%% ============================================================
38	\subsection{Quality Estimation Results}
39	\label{sec:qe_results}
40	
41	\begin{table*}[t]
42	\centering
43	\small
44	\caption{Quality estimation across tasks and models (Spearman $\rho$ and AUROC). All results use $N{=}8$ samples at $T{=}1.0$. Best value per column in \textbf{bold}. SciERC evaluates joint NER (6 types) and RE (7 types); CoNLL evaluates NER (4 types) with two model families.}
45	\label{tab:quality_estimation}
46	\begin{tabular}{ll cc cc cc cc}
47	\toprule
48	& & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{SciERC NER}} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{SciERC RE}} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{CoNLL (Qwen)}} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{CoNLL (LLaMA)}} \\
49	\cmidrule(lr){3-4} \cmidrule(lr){5-6} \cmidrule(lr){7-8} \cmidrule(lr){9-10}
50	Signal & Family & $\rho$ & AUC & $\rho$ & AUC & $\rho$ & AUC & $\rho$ & AUC \\
51	\midrule
52	Voting Conf. & Structural & \textbf{.502} & \textbf{.728} & \textbf{.422} & \textbf{.716} & .424 & .789 & .426 & .709 \\
53	Soft Jaccard  & Structural & .357 & .666 & .211 & .582 & .436 & .801 & \textbf{.431} & .704 \\
54	Fleiss' $\kappa$ & Surface & .265 & .624 & .253 & .631 & .400 & .774 & .428 & .703 \\
55	Exact Match  & Surface    & .257 & .623 & .100 & .504 & \textbf{.451} & \textbf{.816} & \textbf{.431} & .705 \\
56	Log-prob     & Model      & .140 & .559 & .247 & .635 & .316 & .753 & .307 & \textbf{.761} \\
57	\bottomrule
58	\end{tabular}
59	\end{table*}
60	
61	Table~\ref{tab:quality_estimation} presents rank correlation ($\rho$) and AUROC for five confidence signals across tasks and models.
62	
63	\paragraph{Structural signals dominate on complex schemas.}
64	On SciERC NER, Voting Confidence achieves $\rho{=}0.502$, substantially outperforming the second-best signal, SJ ($\rho{=}0.357$), and all remaining signals ($\rho{\leq}0.265$).
65	Voting's advantage reflects its extraction-level granularity: it rewards entities that appear consistently while penalizing hallucinated or missed ones, whereas SJ compares entire sets and is sensitive to both overlap and total extraction count.
66	The structural advantage persists on RE, where Voting ($\rho{=}0.422$) again leads.
67	However, all signals weaken on RE: 44\% of instances receive zero F1, creating a floor effect that compresses the discriminable range.
68	Notably, FK ($\rho{=}0.253$) exceeds SJ ($\rho{=}0.211$) on RE---a reversal from NER that shows no single structural signal dominates across both tasks.
69	
70	\paragraph{Signal rankings shift with task difficulty.}
71	On CoNLL NER, where greedy decoding achieves ${>}$91\% micro F1, the signal landscape changes substantially.
72	Exact Match leads with $\rho{=}0.451$ and AUROC${=}0.816$, surpassing SJ ($\rho{=}0.436$) and Voting ($\rho{=}0.424$).
73	When most samples are near-correct, binary agreement captures the remaining variance more efficiently than set-level similarity.
74	This reversal---EM${>}$SJ on easy tasks vs.\ SJ${>}$EM on hard tasks---demonstrates that optimal signal choice depends on intrinsic task difficulty.
75	
76	\paragraph{Cross-model stability.}
77	Comparing Qwen and LLaMA on CoNLL, SJ shows remarkable stability: $\rho{=}0.436$ (Qwen) vs.\ $\rho{=}0.431$ (LLaMA), a gap of only 0.005.
78	This model-agnostic property is expected for structural signals that operate on outputs rather than internal model states, and provides the strongest evidence that SJ generalizes across architectures.
79	The SJ--FK gap also narrows with schema simplification: $\Delta\rho{=}0.092$ on SciERC NER (6 entity types) vs.\ $\Delta\rho{=}0.003$ on CoNLL with LLaMA (4 types), suggesting that set-level structure contributes less when the type inventory is small.
80	
81	\paragraph{The logprob paradox.}
82	Log-probability reveals a dissociation between ranking and classification.
83	On CoNLL with LLaMA, it achieves the highest AUROC (0.761) yet the lowest $\rho$ (0.307) among all signals.
84	This pattern indicates that logprob assigns well-separated scores to easy vs.\ hard instances (strong binary discrimination) but provides little resolution within each group (weak ranking), making it better suited for binary filtering than continuous quality estimation.
85	We return to this distinction in \S\ref{sec:complexity_robustness} and visualize it in Figure~\ref{fig:signal_heatmap}.
86	
87	\paragraph{Oracle headroom and practical ceilings.}
88	On CoNLL, oracle best-of-$N$ selection yields only +4.2~pp (Qwen) and +1.8~pp (LLaMA) over greedy.
89	When the model already operates near its performance ceiling, confidence signals serve as \textit{reliability assurance}---confirming that outputs are trustworthy---rather than enabling selective prediction gains.
90	We therefore focus selection analysis (\S\ref{sec:selection_gap}) on SciERC, where oracle headroom exceeds 16~pp.
91	
92	%% ============================================================
93	\subsection{The Correlation-Selection Gap}
94	\label{sec:selection_gap}
95	
96	\begin{table}[t]
97	\centering
98	\small
99	\caption{Best-of-$N$ selection F1 on SciERC ($N{=}8$, $T{=}1.0$). Best non-oracle result per column in \textbf{bold}. EM produces binary agreement without sample ranking.}
100	\label{tab:selection}
101	\begin{tabular}{lcc}
102	\toprule
103	Method & NER F1 & RE F1 \\
104	\midrule
105	Oracle & 0.769 & 0.561 \\
106	\midrule
107	Log-prob           & 0.609 & \textbf{0.397} \\
108	Ensemble (SJ+Vot.) & 0.604 & 0.367 \\
109	Soft Jaccard       & 0.604 & 0.368 \\
110	Voting             & 0.596 & 0.338 \\
111	Exact Match        & ---   & ---   \\
112	\midrule
113	Greedy ($T{=}0$)   & \textbf{0.609} & 0.374 \\
114	Random             & 0.580 & 0.338 \\
115	\bottomrule
116	\end{tabular}
117	\end{table}
118	
119	Despite strong quality estimation, confidence signals yield limited gains when used for best-of-$N$ selection.
120	Table~\ref{tab:selection} compares selection F1 on SciERC ($N{=}8$).
121	
122	\paragraph{NER: no signal surpasses greedy.}
123	The oracle upper bound (0.769) reveals 16.0~pp of headroom above greedy (0.609).
124	Yet no confidence signal closes this gap.
125	Log-probability (0.609) merely ties greedy; the best quality estimator, Voting ($\rho{=}0.502$), selects to only 0.596, \textit{below} greedy.
126	An ensemble of SJ and Voting (AUROC${=}0.735$) also fails, achieving 0.604.
127	The greedy--logprob tie is revealing: log-probability selects the sample with highest model confidence, which on average matches the deterministic greedy output, implying that the $N$ samples cluster at a similar quality level with insufficient variance for any signal to exploit.
128	The Random baseline (0.580) confirms that not all samples are equal---uniform selection loses 2.9~pp vs.\ greedy---but the discriminative structure captured by confidence signals adds no value beyond greedy's deterministic choice.
129	
130	\paragraph{RE: logprob uniquely succeeds.}
131	For RE, log-probability is the only signal to exceed greedy (0.397 vs.\ 0.374, +2.3~pp).
132	Structural signals trail or match greedy: SJ selects to 0.368 and Voting to 0.338.
133	The oracle gap of 18.7~pp (0.561 vs.\ 0.374) indicates substantially more per-instance variance than NER.
134	Log-probability's success here may stem from its per-token nature: unlike instance-level consistency signals, logprob evaluates each sample independently, enabling it to distinguish a particularly successful extraction from its peers even when all extractions share similar structural consistency.
135	
136	\paragraph{Quality estimation $\neq$ output selection.}
137	We attribute this gap (Figure~\ref{fig:selection_gap}) to a fundamental distinction: instance-level confidence signals predict \textit{which inputs} the model handles reliably, not \textit{which output} among $N$ candidates is best for a given input.
138	When per-sample variance is low relative to instance-level difficulty---as in NER, where the model often produces $N$ similar extractions---even perfect quality estimation cannot discriminate among near-identical candidates.
139	
140	\paragraph{Implications for test-time scaling.}
141	This correlation-selection gap has direct consequences for test-time scaling in IE \cite{brown2024monkeys, snell2024scaling}.
142	Scaling inference compute through repeated sampling assumes a selector can identify the best sample.
143	Our results show that for structured prediction, existing confidence signals serve as quality \textit{estimators}---useful for flagging unreliable predictions---but not as effective \textit{selectors}.
144	Closing this gap likely requires signals that capture per-sample rather than per-instance variation, such as trained verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers} or pairwise comparison models.
145	
146	%% ============================================================
147	\subsection{Task Complexity and Signal Robustness}
148	\label{sec:complexity_robustness}
149	
150	\paragraph{Task difficulty as a boundary condition.}
151	Signal effectiveness varies systematically with task difficulty.
152	On CoNLL (greedy micro F1${>}$0.91), EM leads all signals ($\rho{=}0.451$); on SciERC NER (micro F1$\,{\approx}\,$0.66), SJ overtakes EM ($\rho{=}0.357$ vs.\ 0.257); on SciERC RE, where 44\% of instances score zero F1, all signals converge to $\rho{\approx}0.25$.
153	The NER--RE difference is statistically confirmed: Fisher's $z$-test on $\rho_\text{SJ}$ yields $z{=}2.31$, $p{=}0.021$.
154	
155	\paragraph{Per-relation diagnostic.}
156	RE signal degradation is relation-specific.
157	\textsc{Feature-Of} has near-zero correlation ($\rho{=}0.004$), while \textsc{Hyponym-Of} achieves $\rho{=}0.646$.
158	The primary bottleneck is entity span errors, which account for 55.5\% of RE false negatives---a prerequisite failure that consistency signals cannot detect, as they measure agreement among equally incorrect extractions.
159

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

\subsection{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:setup}

\paragraph{Datasets.}
We evaluate on three English IE benchmarks spanning a difficulty gradient.
\textbf{SciERC} \cite{luan2018scierc} contains 551 test instances from scientific abstracts annotated for joint NER (6 entity types) and RE (7 relation types), representing a complex schema with overlapping structures.
\textbf{CoNLL-2003} \cite{tjongkimsang2003conll} provides 3{,}453 test sentences from newswire with 4 entity types, serving as a high-accuracy benchmark where models achieve ${>}$91\% micro F1.
\textbf{WNUT-17} \cite{derczynski2017wnut} consists of 1{,}287 test instances from social media with emerging entities, used to probe method boundaries where model capability is insufficient.
This gradient---from near-solved (CoNLL) through challenging (SciERC) to infeasible (WNUT-17)---enables systematic characterization of how signal effectiveness varies with task difficulty (\S\ref{sec:complexity_robustness}).

\paragraph{Models.}
Our primary model is \textbf{Qwen3-8B}, fine-tuned with LoRA ($r{=}32$) separately per dataset.
For cross-model validation, we evaluate \textbf{LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct} to assess whether structural confidence signals transfer across architectures and training regimes.

\paragraph{Sampling and Evaluation.}
For each test instance, we draw $N$ independent samples at temperature $T{=}1.0$, with $T{=}0.7$ for robustness analysis.
We use $N{=}8$ for both SciERC and CoNLL in the primary evaluation, and $N{=}16$ for SciERC scaling experiments.
Quality estimation is measured along two axes: \textit{rank correlation} with instance-level F1 via Spearman $\rho$ and Kendall $\tau$, and \textit{binary discrimination} via AUROC (instances above vs.\ below median F1).
Downstream utility is assessed through \textbf{best-of-$N$ selection F1}: the F1 obtained when each signal selects one sample per instance.
Instance-level F1 uses exact span matching for NER and head-tail-label matching for RE, where a relation is correct only when both argument entities and the relation label match the gold annotation.
The greedy decoding baseline ($T{=}0$, $N{=}1$) establishes performance without test-time scaling.

\paragraph{Confidence Signals.}
We compare five signals from three families (detailed in \S\ref{sec:signals}).
\textit{Structural} signals operate on extracted entity/relation sets: \textbf{Voting Confidence} aggregates per-extraction frequency across samples, and \textbf{Soft Jaccard (SJ)} measures pairwise set similarity \cite{jaccard1901distribution}.
\textit{Surface} signals operate on string representations: \textbf{Fleiss' $\kappa$ (FK)} quantifies inter-sample agreement treating samples as independent annotators \cite{fleiss1971agreement}, and \textbf{Exact Match (EM)} computes the fraction of identical sample pairs.
The \textit{model-internal} signal is \textbf{log-probability (logprob)}, the mean token-level log-likelihood.

\paragraph{Implementation.}
Inference uses vLLM with XGrammar constrained decoding \cite{willard2023guided} to enforce valid JSON output structure.
A span realignment post-processing step corrects character-level offset mismatches between generated and gold annotation spans.
All confidence signals are computed from the $N$ samples without access to gold labels.

%% ============================================================
\subsection{Quality Estimation Results}
\label{sec:qe_results}

\begin{table*}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Quality estimation across tasks and models (Spearman $\rho$ and AUROC). All results use $N{=}8$ samples at $T{=}1.0$. Best value per column in \textbf{bold}. SciERC evaluates joint NER (6 types) and RE (7 types); CoNLL evaluates NER (4 types) with two model families.}
\label{tab:quality_estimation}
\begin{tabular}{ll cc cc cc cc}
\toprule
& & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{SciERC NER}} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{SciERC RE}} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{CoNLL (Qwen)}} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{CoNLL (LLaMA)}} \\
\cmidrule(lr){3-4} \cmidrule(lr){5-6} \cmidrule(lr){7-8} \cmidrule(lr){9-10}
Signal & Family & $\rho$ & AUC & $\rho$ & AUC & $\rho$ & AUC & $\rho$ & AUC \\
\midrule
Voting Conf. & Structural & \textbf{.502} & \textbf{.728} & \textbf{.422} & \textbf{.716} & .424 & .789 & .426 & .709 \\
Soft Jaccard  & Structural & .357 & .666 & .211 & .582 & .436 & .801 & \textbf{.431} & .704 \\
Fleiss' $\kappa$ & Surface & .265 & .624 & .253 & .631 & .400 & .774 & .428 & .703 \\
Exact Match  & Surface    & .257 & .623 & .100 & .504 & \textbf{.451} & \textbf{.816} & \textbf{.431} & .705 \\
Log-prob     & Model      & .140 & .559 & .247 & .635 & .316 & .753 & .307 & \textbf{.761} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table*}

Table~\ref{tab:quality_estimation} presents rank correlation ($\rho$) and AUROC for five confidence signals across tasks and models.

\paragraph{Structural signals dominate on complex schemas.}
On SciERC NER, Voting Confidence achieves $\rho{=}0.502$, substantially outperforming the second-best signal, SJ ($\rho{=}0.357$), and all remaining signals ($\rho{\leq}0.265$).
Voting's advantage reflects its extraction-level granularity: it rewards entities that appear consistently while penalizing hallucinated or missed ones, whereas SJ compares entire sets and is sensitive to both overlap and total extraction count.
The structural advantage persists on RE, where Voting ($\rho{=}0.422$) again leads.
However, all signals weaken on RE: 44\% of instances receive zero F1, creating a floor effect that compresses the discriminable range.
Notably, FK ($\rho{=}0.253$) exceeds SJ ($\rho{=}0.211$) on RE---a reversal from NER that shows no single structural signal dominates across both tasks.

\paragraph{Signal rankings shift with task difficulty.}
On CoNLL NER, where greedy decoding achieves ${>}$91\% micro F1, the signal landscape changes substantially.
Exact Match leads with $\rho{=}0.451$ and AUROC${=}0.816$, surpassing SJ ($\rho{=}0.436$) and Voting ($\rho{=}0.424$).
When most samples are near-correct, binary agreement captures the remaining variance more efficiently than set-level similarity.
This reversal---EM${>}$SJ on easy tasks vs.\ SJ${>}$EM on hard tasks---demonstrates that optimal signal choice depends on intrinsic task difficulty.

\paragraph{Cross-model stability.}
Comparing Qwen and LLaMA on CoNLL, SJ shows remarkable stability: $\rho{=}0.436$ (Qwen) vs.\ $\rho{=}0.431$ (LLaMA), a gap of only 0.005.
This model-agnostic property is expected for structural signals that operate on outputs rather than internal model states, and provides the strongest evidence that SJ generalizes across architectures.
The SJ--FK gap also narrows with schema simplification: $\Delta\rho{=}0.092$ on SciERC NER (6 entity types) vs.\ $\Delta\rho{=}0.003$ on CoNLL with LLaMA (4 types), suggesting that set-level structure contributes less when the type inventory is small.

\paragraph{The logprob paradox.}
Log-probability reveals a dissociation between ranking and classification.
On CoNLL with LLaMA, it achieves the highest AUROC (0.761) yet the lowest $\rho$ (0.307) among all signals.
This pattern indicates that logprob assigns well-separated scores to easy vs.\ hard instances (strong binary discrimination) but provides little resolution within each group (weak ranking), making it better suited for binary filtering than continuous quality estimation.
We return to this distinction in \S\ref{sec:complexity_robustness} and visualize it in Figure~\ref{fig:signal_heatmap}.

\paragraph{Oracle headroom and practical ceilings.}
On CoNLL, oracle best-of-$N$ selection yields only +4.2~pp (Qwen) and +1.8~pp (LLaMA) over greedy.
When the model already operates near its performance ceiling, confidence signals serve as \textit{reliability assurance}---confirming that outputs are trustworthy---rather than enabling selective prediction gains.
We therefore focus selection analysis (\S\ref{sec:selection_gap}) on SciERC, where oracle headroom exceeds 16~pp.

%% ============================================================
\subsection{The Correlation-Selection Gap}
\label{sec:selection_gap}

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Best-of-$N$ selection F1 on SciERC ($N{=}8$, $T{=}1.0$). Best non-oracle result per column in \textbf{bold}. EM produces binary agreement without sample ranking.}
\label{tab:selection}
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
Method & NER F1 & RE F1 \\
\midrule
Oracle & 0.769 & 0.561 \\
\midrule
Log-prob           & 0.609 & \textbf{0.397} \\
Ensemble (SJ+Vot.) & 0.604 & 0.367 \\
Soft Jaccard       & 0.604 & 0.368 \\
Voting             & 0.596 & 0.338 \\
Exact Match        & ---   & ---   \\
\midrule
Greedy ($T{=}0$)   & \textbf{0.609} & 0.374 \\
Random             & 0.580 & 0.338 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Despite strong quality estimation, confidence signals yield limited gains when used for best-of-$N$ selection.
Table~\ref{tab:selection} compares selection F1 on SciERC ($N{=}8$).

\paragraph{NER: no signal surpasses greedy.}
The oracle upper bound (0.769) reveals 16.0~pp of headroom above greedy (0.609).
Yet no confidence signal closes this gap.
Log-probability (0.609) merely ties greedy; the best quality estimator, Voting ($\rho{=}0.502$), selects to only 0.596, \textit{below} greedy.
An ensemble of SJ and Voting (AUROC${=}0.735$) also fails, achieving 0.604.
The greedy--logprob tie is revealing: log-probability selects the sample with highest model confidence, which on average matches the deterministic greedy output, implying that the $N$ samples cluster at a similar quality level with insufficient variance for any signal to exploit.
The Random baseline (0.580) confirms that not all samples are equal---uniform selection loses 2.9~pp vs.\ greedy---but the discriminative structure captured by confidence signals adds no value beyond greedy's deterministic choice.

\paragraph{RE: logprob uniquely succeeds.}
For RE, log-probability is the only signal to exceed greedy (0.397 vs.\ 0.374, +2.3~pp).
Structural signals trail or match greedy: SJ selects to 0.368 and Voting to 0.338.
The oracle gap of 18.7~pp (0.561 vs.\ 0.374) indicates substantially more per-instance variance than NER.
Log-probability's success here may stem from its per-token nature: unlike instance-level consistency signals, logprob evaluates each sample independently, enabling it to distinguish a particularly successful extraction from its peers even when all extractions share similar structural consistency.

\paragraph{Quality estimation $\neq$ output selection.}
We attribute this gap (Figure~\ref{fig:selection_gap}) to a fundamental distinction: instance-level confidence signals predict \textit{which inputs} the model handles reliably, not \textit{which output} among $N$ candidates is best for a given input.
When per-sample variance is low relative to instance-level difficulty---as in NER, where the model often produces $N$ similar extractions---even perfect quality estimation cannot discriminate among near-identical candidates.

\paragraph{Implications for test-time scaling.}
This correlation-selection gap has direct consequences for test-time scaling in IE \cite{brown2024monkeys, snell2024scaling}.
Scaling inference compute through repeated sampling assumes a selector can identify the best sample.
Our results show that for structured prediction, existing confidence signals serve as quality \textit{estimators}---useful for flagging unreliable predictions---but not as effective \textit{selectors}.
Closing this gap likely requires signals that capture per-sample rather than per-instance variation, such as trained verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers} or pairwise comparison models.

%% ============================================================
\subsection{Task Complexity and Signal Robustness}
\label{sec:complexity_robustness}

\paragraph{Task difficulty as a boundary condition.}
Signal effectiveness varies systematically with task difficulty.
On CoNLL (greedy micro F1${>}$0.91), EM leads all signals ($\rho{=}0.451$); on SciERC NER (micro F1$\,{\approx}\,$0.66), SJ overtakes EM ($\rho{=}0.357$ vs.\ 0.257); on SciERC RE, where 44\% of instances score zero F1, all signals converge to $\rho{\approx}0.25$.
The NER--RE difference is statistically confirmed: Fisher's $z$-test on $\rho_\text{SJ}$ yields $z{=}2.31$, $p{=}0.021$.

\paragraph{Per-relation diagnostic.}
RE signal degradation is relation-specific.
\textsc{Feature-Of} has near-zero correlation ($\rho{=}0.004$), while \textsc{Hyponym-Of} achieves $\rho{=}0.646$.
The primary bottleneck is entity span errors, which account for 55.5\% of RE false negatives---a prerequisite failure that consistency signals cannot detect, as they measure agreement among equally incorrect extractions.

\paragraph{Capability stratification.}
SJ effectiveness scales with structural complexity: on SciERC instances with 6+ entities, $\rho{=}0.547$, compared to $\rho{=}0.415$ for 1--2 entities.
The SJ advantage over logprob remains stable across sentence-length quartiles ($\Delta\rho{\approx}0.08$--$0.20$), and three independent complexity proxies (entity count, sentence length, relation density) show weak mutual correlation ($|r|{<}0.15$), indicating a genuinely multi-dimensional benefit rather than a single confound.

\paragraph{Method boundary: WNUT-17.}
WNUT-17 establishes where the approach breaks down.
SJ achieves $\rho{=}0.062$ ($p{=}0.106$, not statistically significant), with 54\% of instances at zero F1.
Log-probability shows a strong \textit{negative} correlation ($\rho{=}{-}0.411$): the model is confidently wrong on novel entities, a calibration failure that no post-hoc consistency signal can remedy.
This is a boundary of the method, not a limitation of the datasets.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Signal robustness across temperature and sample size on SciERC (Spearman $\rho$). $^\dagger$Mean over 3 seeds ($\sigma{=}0.025$; individual: 0.428, 0.424, 0.384).}
\label{tab:robustness}
\begin{tabular}{llcc}
\toprule
& & NER $\rho$ & RE $\rho$ \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{4}{l}{\textit{Temperature} ($N{=}8$)} \\
\quad SJ & $T{=}0.7$ & 0.388 & 0.234 \\
\quad SJ & $T{=}1.0$ & 0.357 & 0.211 \\
\quad FK & $T{=}0.7$ & 0.321 & 0.184 \\
\quad FK & $T{=}1.0$ & 0.265 & 0.253 \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{4}{l}{\textit{Sample size} ($T{=}1.0$)} \\
\quad SJ & $N{=}8$  & 0.357 & 0.211 \\
\quad SJ & $N{=}16$ & 0.412$^\dagger$ & 0.281 \\
\quad FK & $N{=}8$  & 0.265 & 0.253 \\
\quad FK & $N{=}16$ & 0.280 & 0.279 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Robustness analysis.}
Table~\ref{tab:robustness} reports signal stability across temperature and sample size on SciERC.
\textit{Temperature.}
SJ NER $\rho$ shifts from 0.388 ($T{=}0.7$) to 0.357 ($T{=}1.0$), a difference of 0.031 whose bootstrap confidence interval includes zero.
FK shows mixed behavior: NER $\rho$ drops by 0.056, while RE $\rho$ increases by 0.069, likely reflecting reduced diversity at lower temperature interacting differently across tasks.
Across all comparisons, the SJ--FK relative ordering is preserved at both temperatures on NER (0.388 vs.\ 0.321 at $T{=}0.7$; 0.357 vs.\ 0.265 at $T{=}1.0$), indicating a stable signal hierarchy despite numerically small temperature effects.

\textit{Sample size.}
Increasing from $N{=}8$ to $N{=}16$ yields meaningful gains for SJ on NER: $\rho$ improves from 0.357 to $0.412{\pm}0.025$ (three seeds: 0.428, 0.424, 0.384).
FK benefits less ($\rho{\approx}0.280$ at $N{=}16$ vs.\ 0.265 at $N{=}8$).
For RE at $N{=}16$, SJ ($\rho{=}0.281$), FK ($\rho{=}0.279$), and logprob ($\rho{=}0.287$) all plateau at comparable levels, suggesting that compound entity-then-relation errors impose a ceiling that additional samples cannot overcome.

\paragraph{Cross-model transfer.}
LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct replicates the structural-over-surface ordering on SciERC NER (SJ $\rho{=}0.363$, FK $\rho{=}0.327$).
On CoNLL, the cross-model gap is minimal (Table~\ref{tab:quality_estimation}): SJ achieves $\rho{=}0.431$ (LLaMA) vs.\ 0.436 (Qwen), $\Delta{=}0.005$.
On conditional RE (non-zero F1 instances), SJ recovers to $\rho{=}0.405$ while FK drops to $\rho{=}0.259$, confirming that structural advantage is robust across both models and evaluation conditions.

\paragraph{Evaluation circularity.}
Leave-one-out SJ (LOO-SJ), which excludes the target sample when computing confidence, yields $\Delta\rho{=}{-}0.014$ relative to standard SJ, with a maximum per-instance $\Delta\rho$ of $3.1{\times}10^{-4}$.
Evaluation circularity is negligible.

\paragraph{Conditional filtering reveals signal divergence.}
Filtering to non-zero F1 instances improves SJ correlations: NER $\rho{=}0.412$ (from 0.357), RE $\rho{=}0.368$ at $N{=}8$.
